title: Toward a Science of Translating (Eugene A. Nida, 1964)
supports: Bibliographic record (Brill, 1964; subjects: translating, Bible translating); source of the formal and dynamic equivalence ideas summarised in the canon

title: Translating as a Purposeful Activity: Functionalist Approaches Explained (Christiane Nord, 1997)
supports: Bibliographic record (St. Jerome, 1997; later Taylor & Francis edition); the functionalist, purpose-first approach summarised in the canon

title: The Translator's Invisibility: A History of Translation (Lawrence Venuti, 1995)
supports: Bibliographic record (Routledge, 1995); source of the domestication and foreignisation ideas summarised in the canon

title: Global communications - Microsoft Writing Style Guide
supports: Definitions: translation changes the language and is often automated; localization adapts content to a locale's language, cultural and political expectations and is done by people who know the culture (page updated 15 Oct 2026)

title: Microsoft Localization Style Guides
supports: Free per-language style guides covering localization guidelines, language style and usage, and market-specific data formats, for about 100 languages and variants

title: Localization vs. Internationalization
supports: What localization adapts (number, date and time formats, currency, sorting, symbols, colours, culturally sensitive text and images, legal requirements) and how internationalization makes it possible

title: Language tags in HTML and XML
supports: BCP 47 language tags (RFC 5646), subtag order, advice to keep tags short, examples zh-Hans, es-419, en-GB

title: Unicode CLDR Project
supports: CLDR supplies date, number, currency and unit formats, sorting and plural rules used by operating systems, browsers and languages; CLDR 49 released 2026-10-22

title: Language Plural Rules (CLDR charts)
supports: Cardinal plural categories: English one/other; French one/many/other; Polish and Russian one/few/many/other; Arabic six categories; Japanese other only

title: Intl.NumberFormat
supports: Same number formatted by locale: de-DE 123.456,789; en-IN 1,23,456.789 (lakh grouping); yen shown with no minor unit (page modified 10 Jul 2025)

title: Personal names around the world
supports: Name order varies, some people have no family name, avoid 'first name' and 'last name' labels, allow long names and Unicode

title: Structural markup and right-to-left text in HTML
supports: Set dir="rtl" on the html element, not in CSS; use logical start and end values; dir="auto" and bdi for user text

title: Tell Google about localized versions of your page
supports: hreflang by HTML, HTTP header or sitemap; every version lists itself and the others; x-default; ISO 639-1 and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes; es-419 not supported; reserved codes such as UK have no effect

title: Managing multi-regional and multilingual sites
supports: Google reads language from visible content, not lang attributes; one language per page; avoid automatic redirects by language; URL structure options; URL parameters not recommended

title: Spam policies for Google web search
supports: Scaled content abuse includes generating many pages by automated transformations such as translating scraped content that gives users little value

title: Glossaries (DeepL API reference)
supports: Glossaries from TSV or CSV term pairs, v3 multilingual glossaries, limits (10 MiB per glossary, 1024 bytes per entry, 1000 glossaries per account)

title: Create and use glossaries (Cloud Translation Advanced)
supports: Unidirectional (TSV, CSV, TMX) and equivalent-term-set glossaries; size limits; case-sensitive matching; contextual glossary translation only with Translation LLM; glossaries are not versioned, so keep the source files

title: Translation Memory
supports: How a translation memory stores segments, Perfect, 100% and fuzzy matches, TMX/XLSX/CSV import and export up to 200 MB, auto-translation via TM using only 100% and Perfect matches

title: XLIFF Version 2.1 (OASIS Standard)
supports: XLIFF 2.1 (OASIS Standard, 13 February 2018) carries localizable content between tools in the localization process

title: MQM (Multidimensional Quality Metrics)
supports: Analytic translation quality evaluation with a shared error typology (accuracy, fluency, terminology, style and more), severities and scores; aligned with ISO 5060

title: Findings of the WMT25 General Machine Translation Shared Task: Time to Stop Evaluating on Easy Test Sets (Kocmi et al., 2025)
supports: Nov 2025 results: 30 language pairs, 60 systems, human evaluation on half; best system in the top cluster for 14 of 16 pairs; human references in the winning cluster for 6 of 15; automatic metrics biased; weaknesses with terminology, non-standard input, gender and low-resource languages (PDF read)

title: Guidelines on transparency obligations for providers and deployers of AI systems
supports: Commission guidelines on AI Act Article 50, published 20 July 2026 and updated 5 November 2026; the transparency obligations apply from 2 August 2026

title: Labelling AI-Generated Content: What Article 50 of the AI Act Actually Requires of Translation (MQM RFC-1)
publisher: MQM Council (summary, not the official text)
supports: Secondary summary dated 2 Aug 2026, used because the Commission landing page does not show the detail: machine translation treated as editing for the provider marking duty; deployer label for public-interest text unless human review and editorial responsibility; each translated version needs its own review

title: Content Guidelines (AI-generated content)
supports: Authors must disclose AI-generated content, including translations created by an AI tool, even if edited afterwards; AI-assisted work need not be disclosed

title: Tips for Filing Forms by Mail
supports: Foreign-language documents need a complete English translation certified as complete and accurate, with the translator's certification of competence (page updated 10 Jul 2026)

title: Certifying a document
supports: For documents not in English or Welsh, the translator confirms in writing that it is a true and accurate translation, with the date, full name and contact details

title: Guidance on Certified Translations
supports: What a UK certified translation certificate contains; use a qualified translator or company affiliated to CIOL, ITI or ATC; public registers to find one

title: Getting your public documents accepted in the EU
supports: Multilingual standard forms can replace translations of covered public documents; a certified translation may be asked for only exceptionally; no apostille for covered documents (page last checked 17 Feb 2026)

title: English (USA) Timed Text Style Guide
supports: English subtitles: 42 characters per line; reading speed up to 20 characters per second for adult and 17 for children's programmes

title: Timed Text Style Guide: General Requirements
supports: Two lines maximum per subtitle; minimum duration five-sixths of a second; maximum seven seconds per subtitle event
